builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
summary: EnvOpt replaces hand-designed agent environments (tool outputs, document layouts, data-source representations) with automatically optimized environment configurations, requiring no graders or reference answers and using real or synthetic tasks. The cost is an offline optimization loop that consumes API or GPU inference budget, plus the engineering effort to expose the environment as a tunable surface and to build representative tasks. It can fail when the synthetic or sampled tasks do not match the production task distribution, when the optimized environment overfits to one benchmark and degrades under environment drift, or when undocumented rejected strategies silently hurt accuracy on unseen task types.
rationale: The method targets exactly the reader's setting (API-based agents, no training) with reported cost reductions transferable across models and harnesses, but the gains are benchmark-specific and the optimization loop itself costs money, so it must be validated on the reader's actual environment before adoption.

claims.statement: EnvOpt replaces hand-designed agent environments (tool outputs, document layouts, data-source representations) with automatically optimized environment configurations, requiring no graders or reference answers and using real or synthetic tasks. The cost is an offline optimization loop that consumes API or GPU inference budget, plus the engineering effort to expose the environment as a tunable surface and to build representative tasks. It can fail when the synthetic or sampled tasks do not match the production task distribution, when the optimized environment overfits to one benchmark and degrades under environment drift, or when undocumented rejected strategies silently hurt accuracy on unseen task types.

On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces Claude Haiku 4.5 cost by 72.7% while raising pass rate by 14.34 percentage points; the optimized environment transfers to Opus 5 (68.1% cost cut) and stacks on Meta-Harness for a further 83.4% cost reduction, with results across 5 benchmarks.
